title: Who Could Support Public Work?
definition: Taking part in matters affecting a wider community.
imageAlt: Three teaching cards connect work and resources, study and useful skills, and public participation. Resources are shown as opportunities, not a measure of human worth.
content:
The museum needs a new exhibit: who helped bring public concerns into discussion? Start with the emerging middle class. Some families involved in business, farming or professional work had resources to support study and public activities. The group was varied. Its members did not all have the same income, experience or opinion.

Resources could help pay for books, travel, printing or time to study. Education could develop skills used in writing, translation and organized requests. These are connections to investigate, not a rule that only wealthy people could think or contribute. Work and knowledge within local communities also mattered.

Your exhibit will follow three actions: translating an article, producing a regional newspaper and requesting a school. Ask who acted, what skill or support the action needed, and which public concern it addressed.
clues: Resources
Books, fees, travel and printing can require time, money or support.
Skills
Writing and translation can help people participate in public discussion.
People and contributions
Investigate actions and concerns instead of ranking people by wealth.
task: Which connection should the new exhibit explain?
How resources and skills could support writing, translation and organized requests.
How the price of a book measured its reader's human worth.
Why only people who travelled could discuss a public concern.
Why a profession made every person hold the same opinion.
reason: Resources and education could support public work. To understand a contribution, connect a person's action with the public concern it addressed.

title: A Translation Reaches More Readers
definition: Expressing a message in another language.
imageAlt: A modern diagram connects Rizal's Spanish-language Amor Patrio in 1882 with del Pilar's Tagalog translation and a Tagalog-reading audience. It is not a facsimile of a newspaper.
content:
In 1882, Diariong Tagalog published material in Tagalog and Spanish. It included Rizal's essay Amor Patrio and Marcelo H. del Pilar's Tagalog translation. A bilingual newspaper uses two languages.

Why translate? A reader who understands Tagalog but cannot read Spanish can use the Tagalog version. The action connects a text with a possible audience. It does not tell us exactly how many people read it or that every reader agreed. Think about the skill involved: the translator must understand a message and express its meaning for another audience.

For the museum task, choose the label that identifies del Pilar's action. Rizal wrote the essay; del Pilar supplied the Tagalog translation. Both roles matter, and they are different. We use a labelled teaching diagram rather than pretend that the cards are original newspaper pages.
clues: The publication
Diariong Tagalog printed Tagalog and Spanish material in 1882.
Different roles
Rizal wrote Amor Patrio; del Pilar translated it into Tagalog.
Possible audience
Translation made the ideas available in Tagalog to people able to read that language.
task: Which contribution belongs with del Pilar's translation?
Making the essay available in Tagalog for Tagalog readers.
Opening an Iloilo shipping route to Melbourne.
Requesting permission for the Malolos school.
Founding the Suez Canal as a student project.
reason: Translation connects a written message with readers of another language. Identify the essay writer and translator as distinct contributors.

title: A Regional Newspaper Is Public Work
definition: A person who prepares and organizes material for a publication.
imageAlt: Three modern cards identify Isabelo de los Reyes, El Ilocano in 1889, and the action of preparing a newspaper. They do not reproduce an original issue or claim universal readership.
content:
Another case brings regional experience into the exhibit. Isabelo de los Reyes was born in Vigan, Ilocos Sur. He founded El Ilocano in 1889. A newspaper needs writing, editing and production. Its creation is a concrete example of public work connected with education and communication.

Do not merge two publications because both were newspapers. Diariong Tagalog belongs to the 1882 translation case. El Ilocano belongs to the 1889 publishing case involving de los Reyes. Give each its own name, person, date and action.

A regional contribution need not happen in Europe to belong in the story of public discussion. At the same time, founding a newspaper is not evidence that everyone in a region read it. Our task is to identify what the record establishes and explain how publishing can create a space for written ideas.
clues: Person and place
Isabelo de los Reyes came from Vigan, Ilocos Sur.
Publication and year
He founded El Ilocano in 1889.
Action
Publishing requires people to prepare and share written material.
task: Which label correctly identifies this regional publishing case?
Isabelo de los Reyes founded El Ilocano in 1889.
The Malolos women founded El Ilocano during their 1888 request.
Del Pilar built the Suez Canal for the 1882 newspaper.
The Iloilo machinery shipment was an issue of El Ilocano.
reason: Keep the named person, publication and date together. Regional publishing is an example of public participation within the Philippines.

title: The Malolos Women Ask for Schooling
definition: A formal request asking an authority to act.
imageAlt: A teaching sequence identifies Malolos women, a request dated 12 December 1888, and the aim of a self-funded Spanish-language night school. The request is distinguished from a proven outcome.
content:
In Malolos, Bulacan, women took an organized step for their education. The historical marker records their request to Governor-General Weyler on 12 December 1888 for permission to open a Spanish-language night school at their own expense.

The important action here is the request. The women were participants with an educational goal, not merely people waiting for someone else to think for them. Preparing a request and arranging support for schooling were forms of public action. This example also helps us ask how duties, costs and access shaped learning opportunities.

The marker records that Rizal later wrote to praise their initiative. A later letter of support is different from the women's earlier request. In your exhibit, give the initiative to the people who made it. This scene studies a documented request; it does not ask students to disclose family finances or imitate a historical petition to a real official.
clues: Place and action
Malolos women requested permission for a school in Bulacan.
1888 request
The marker dates their request to 12 December 1888 and describes their own funding.
Initiative and support
Their request came before Rizal's later letter praising their initiative.
task: What action should the exhibit attribute to the Malolos women?
Organizing a request for permission to open their own Spanish-language school.
Translating Amor Patrio for Diariong Tagalog in 1882.
Founding El Ilocano in 1889.
Opening Iloilo Port to international trade in 1855.
reason: The women made the educational request themselves. A later supportive letter should not erase their initiative or be confused with the original request.

title: Build the Contribution Exhibit
definition: An action or support that helps a shared effort.
imageAlt: Three modern exhibit cards identify translation, a regional newspaper and a school request as different actions. Students must connect each with its contribution before explaining.
content:
You now have three sourced cases. Del Pilar translated a text so it could be available in Tagalog. De los Reyes founded El Ilocano. The Malolos women requested permission for a school. The cases show different ways people used skills, organization and support to take part in public life.

Build the exhibit by matching each action with its contribution. Match the evidence, not the person's fame or wealth. The translation concerns language access. The newspaper concerns preparing a publication. The request concerns an attempt to expand schooling.

These actions did not all happen in one year or guarantee the same result. A request is an action toward a goal; a publication makes material available but does not prove every reader's response. After the matches fit, explain why more than one kind of contribution belongs in the exhibit.
clues: Translation
Connect another language version with possible readers of that language.
Publication
Connect founding a newspaper with creating a place for written material.
School request
Connect an organized educational request with an attempt to expand access.
task: Why should the exhibit include all three kinds of action?
They show distinct ways people participated in public concerns.
Only the best-known writer should receive credit for every action.
A school request and a newspaper must have identical outcomes.
All contributors had to study abroad before they could act.
reason: Public participation took different forms. Explain each person or group's actual action and the concern it addressed.

title: Explain the Exhibit to Another Learner
definition: Taking a step to begin or improve something.
imageAlt: A selected timeline orders the 1882 translation, the Malolos women's 1888 request and El Ilocano in 1889. The labels keep distinct contributors and actions attached to the dates.
content:
Prepare a short explanation for another Grade 5 learner. Start with an action, then connect it with a public concern. Try: Del Pilar contributed by ___. De los Reyes contributed by ___. The Malolos women contributed by ___. Resources and education could help people ___.

Keep the selected dates in order: the translation appeared in 1882, the Malolos request was made in 1888, and El Ilocano was founded in 1889. Explain the connection instead of only reciting years. Writers, translators and organized learners made different contributions. Their examples do not mean everyone had equal resources or that people without travel opportunities lacked knowledge.

The five-question quiz checks ideas taught in these scenes. Review a difficult scene, try targeted practice and retry when ready. Passing earns this mission's reward once. Chapter 15 remains partial; its final challenge is not available yet.
clues: Diariong Tagalog includes the essay and Tagalog translation.
The Malolos women make their school request.
De los Reyes founds El Ilocano.
task: Which explanation gives contributors their distinct roles?
A translator, a regional publisher and organized women learners used different actions for public concerns.
The same person performed all three actions in 1882.
Every contribution depended on studying in Madrid.
The school request proves every family had equal access to education.
reason: Keep people, actions, dates and concerns connected. Different opportunities and forms of participation belong in the explanation.
